children: By Sona Nambiar

Shaza Hotels expects the estimated asset value of properties to double to approximately $800 million by 2030, supported by plans to add 15 hotels over the next five years, a senior executive told Zawya Projects.
The UAE-headquartered hospitality management company, owned by Qatar's Barwa Real Estate Group, operates under two brands: the five-star Shaza Hotels and the four-star Mysk by Shaz

“Currently, Shaza operates and manages almost a $400 million portfolio with the coming pipeline, and we plan to add another 15 hotels in the coming five years, making it 30+ hotels and branded residences based on market demand by 2030,” said Vice President of Business Development & Growth Shaji Abu Salih.
“We expect to make it $800 million worth of assets by 2030, which we will be managing and operating on behalf of owners and investors,” he said.
As a niche luxury brand, the company takes a cautious and selective approach to expansion, the senior executive said.

“So most of our investments are strategically decided after seeing the land, sitting with the owner and advising on the investment, because we are talking about a long-term relationship with contracts for 20-25 years,” he explained.

The luxury hospitality group is expanding its footprint to markets like Turkey, Central Asia and North Africa, which offer strong potential for culturally relevant, family-focused hospitality beyond the company's established GCC base, he disclosed.
Excerpts from the interview:
As a luxury hotel management company, you said you selectively work with owners and investors. Starting 2027, which are your priority markets for expansion?

We are headquartered in the UAE and our brand was created for halal-conscious investors and halal-conscious travellers. Our hospitality group operates and manages properties under two distinct brands: Shaza Hotels (luxury five-star) and Mysk by Shaza (four-star Arabian lifestyle focus).
So we retain the highest concentration of our current portfolio growth in the GCC; currently we are in the midst of discussions for branded residences in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

However, our mass development pipeline is Saudi Arabia, given the country's expanding tourism infrastructure and Vision 2030 plans. While we have a flagship property each in Mecca, Medina, Jeddah and Riyadh with Shaza as the main brand, our strategy is to target the Tier 2 cities, namely Al-Ahsa, Hail, Abha and Tabuk, with our Mysk brand so that it brings a kind of new experiential tourism into those cities, which will fulfill the Vision 2030 of Saudi Arabia.
With the current situation in Saudi Arabia, are you still going ahead with those projects?

Geopolitical tensions are not new to this region. What is happening has impacted our hotels in Saudi Arabia and there might be some realignment where we might take a step back to see whether our course is right or wrong.
But we are working towards a long-term vision, which is mostly futuristic, and our industry will be back because we are resilient and we are supported by the local tourism bodies and government.
What are your plans for the rest of the GCC? Are you exploring any other concepts besides hotels?
We are seeing strong acceptance of the branded residences concept and we have our first one coming up in Oman. We have a few in the pipeline in Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Orlando.

In Oman, we are discussing a 4-star hotel in Muscat as well as a luxury branded residence. In Kuwait, we are in discussions for a city hotel because the country is still not active with the branded residence concept. In Qatar, we might take over a 4-star hotel by the end of this year in Doha as a very quick win.
What about your global forays?

In Turkey, we are looking at a mixed-use complex and we are pursuing leads in Almaty and Bukhara in Uzbekistan. In Orlando, we have a hotel resort and a branded residence under both the brands, Shaza and Mysk. It is a huge complex with other brands and it is going to be a part of a large tourism infrastructure right in front of the parks and the tourism attractions in Orlando.
You also said that you are expanding your footprint to Morocco and Egypt.
It's too early to talk about because we are in discussions with potential owners and investors in Morocco. We are also in talks with some developers in Egypt.
We have also been invited by the government of Maldives as they have shown some interest towards developing halal-friendly hotels and resorts - this is totally new territory for us.
(Reporting by Sona Nambiar; Editing by Anoop Menon)
